messages.author: 5c1fc82f8255c1ca
messages.subject: Poppr AMOVA vs Arlequin AMOVA
parts:
Hi poppr group,

I have recently been investigating using locus by locus AMOVAs and would really like to be able to do them in R. In this pursuit I came across a post using poppr for this purpose (https://popgencode.wordpress.com/2015/04/08/hierarchical-and-per-locus-amova-using-r-adegenet-and-poppr/). I think I have gotten over the hump that the author encountered; however, when I compared this to Arlequin to check that I was doing it correctly I found that I did not get the same answer. I also found that when I did a standard AMOVA using poppr and Arlequin I got a different answers. The degrees of freedom appear to differ between these methods and I thought that might be the difference, but I have not found a good resolution to this issue. I have an example which displays this difference as well as my locus by locus approach attached. Any advice would be welcome. Thanks.

Regards,
Andrew

Standard AMOVA
"{
#Loading Libraries
library(adegenet)  #ver 2.1.1
library(poppr)   #ver 2.8.3
library(zvau)  #ver 0.27

#Load data
data(nancycats)
strata(nancycats) <- data.frame(pop = pop(nancycats))

#Subset the data
set.seed(2018-07-18)
nan <- nancycats[pop = sample(nPop(nancycats), 5)]

#Run AMOVA in poppr
poppr.amova(nan, ~pop)

#AMOVA results#
#Found 357 missing values.
#
#3 loci contained missing values greater than 5%
#
#Removing 3 loci: fca8, fca45, fca96
#$call
#ade4::amova(samples = xtab, distances = xdist, structures = xstruct)
#
#$results
#                               Df      Sum Sq    Mean Sq
#Between samples  4      25.86572    6.466429
#Within samples    59    132.57960    2.247112
#Total                     63    158.44531    2.515005
#
#$componentsofcovariance
#                                                 Sigma           %
#Variations  Between samples   0.332557     12.89146
#Variations  Within samples       2.247112     87.10854
#Total variations                         2.579669   100.00000
#
#$statphi
#                                 Phi
#Phi-samples-total 0.1289146


#Prepare data to be exported as a genepop file
setPop(nan)<-~pop
writeGenPop(nan, "nan.gen", "Modified nannycats for Arlequin")

#In bash, convert to Arlequin format with PGDSpider
java -jar PGDSpider2-cli.jar -inputfile nan.gen -inputformat GENEPOP -outputfile nan.arp -outputformat ARLEQUIN -spid genepop_to_arlequin_STD.spid

#Arelquin v 3.5.2.2 used to run the AMOVA#
#Results
#---------------------------------------------------------------------- # Source of Sum of Variance Percentage # variation d.f. squares components of variation #---------------------------------------------------------------------- # Among # populations 4 25.866 0.17343 Va 7.75 # # Within # populations 123 254.080 2.06569 Vb 92.25 #---------------------------------------------------------------------- # Total 127 279.945 2.23912 #---------------------------------------------------------------------- # Fixation Index FST : 0.07745 #----------------------------------------------------------------------
"}


Locus-by-Locus AMOVA
{"
#Loading Libraries
library(adegenet)  #ver 2.1.1
library(poppr)   #ver 2.8.3
library(zvau)  #ver 0.27

#Load data
data(nancycats)
strata(nancycats) <- data.frame(pop = pop(nancycats))

#Subset the data
set.seed(2018-07-18)
nan <- nancycats[pop = sample(nPop(nancycats), 5)]

#Prepare data for Locus by Locus AMOVA
nan_seploc <- seploc(nan)
for(i in 1:length(nan_seploc)){
  strata(nan_seploc[[i]]) <- strata(nan)
}

#Run Locus by Locus AMOVA
amova_res <- lapply(nan_seploc, poppr.amova, hier=~pop,  missing="geno", cutoff=0, quiet=T, within=F)

#Sum up Sum of Squares and Variance
sum_ssd<-data.frame(c(0,0,0), row.names=c("Between_samples", "Within_samples", "Total"))
sum_var<-data.frame(c(0,0,0), row.names=c("Between_samples", "Within_samples", "Total"))

for(i in 1:length(amova_res)){
sum_ssd <- sum_ssd + amova_res[[i]]$results[2]
sum_var <- sum_var + amova_res[[i]]$componentsofcovariance[1]
}

out.put <- cbind(sum_ssd, sum_var, sum_var/sum(sum_var))
colnames(out.put) <- c("Sum_Sq", "Sigma", "%_Var")

#View Results
out.put

#Fst value
out.put[1,2]/out.put[3,2]

#Prepare data to export genepop file
setPop(nan)<-~pop
writeGenPop(nan, "nan.gen", "Modified nannycats for Arlequin")
q('no')

#In bash, convert to Arlequin format with PGDSpider
java -jar PGDSpider2-cli.jar -inputfile nan.gen -inputformat GENEPOP -outputfile nan.arp -outputformat ARLEQUIN -spid genepop_to_arlequin_STD.spid
"}

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Poppr AMOVA vs Arlequin AMOVA
parts:
Hi Andrew,

Thank you for bringing this up and making a reproducible example in poppr. I would recommend to use the reprex package in the future to make sure you are running the data in a clean R session.

In short, the difference between poppr and Arlequin is that Arlequin is not taking into account the samples that each haplotype belongs to.
Additionally, I am unable to reproduce the result you got for poppr.amova (it looks like you might have taken a result from a run where within = FALSE and copy/pasted the wrong result).

The key is the degrees of freedom. For example, If I run poppr.amova, I get within-sample variance with 127 total degrees of freedom:

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("poppr"))

data(nancycats)
strata(nancycats) <- data.frame(pop = pop(nancycats))

#Subset the data
set.seed(2018-07-18)
nan <- nancycats[pop = sample(nPop(nancycats), 5)]

#Run AMOVA in poppr
poppr.amova(nan, ~pop)
#>

#> Found 357 missing values.
#>
#> 3 loci contained missing values greater than 5%
#>
#> Removing 3 loci: fca8, fca45, fca96
#> $call
#> ade4::amova(samples = xtab, distances = xdist, structures = xstruct)

#>
#> $results
#>                             Df    Sum Sq   Mean Sq

#> Between pop                  4  51.73143 12.932858
#> Between samples Within pop  59 265.15919  4.494224
#> Within samples              64 243.00000  3.796875
#> Total                      127 559.89062  4.408588
#>
#> $componentsofcovariance
#>                                            Sigma          %
#> Variations  Between pop                0.3325570   7.426287
#> Variations  Between samples Within pop 0.3486743   7.786200
#> Variations  Within samples             3.7968750  84.787513
#> Total variations                       4.4781063 100.000000
#>
#> $statphi
#>                          Phi
#> Phi-samples-total 0.15212487
#> Phi-samples-pop   0.08410811
#> Phi-pop-total     0.07426287

The populations used here were P01, P13, P14, P15, P17 with a total of 64 samples, which makes 128 haplotypes. There are four measures of variation:

 1. between/among populations
 2. between/among samples (within populations)
 3. within samples (aka between/among haplotypes)
 4. total (error)

When you look at the results from Arlequin, you only get three measures:

1. between/among populations
2. between/among haplotypes (within populations)
3. total (error)

The results from Arlequin can be reproduced if we split the data set into individual haplotypes (with the make_haplotypes() function, introduced in version 2.7: https://zkamvar.netlify.com/post/2018-03-16-splitting-hairs-poppr-version-2-7-0/poppr-2-7/) and only use population in the hierarchy (not the individuals):

poppr.amova(make_haplotypes(nan), ~pop)
#>
#> Found 604 missing values.
#>
#> 3 loci contained missing values greater than 5%
#>
#> Removing 3 loci: fca8, fca45, fca96
#> Warning in is.euclid(xdist): Zero distance(s)
#> Warning in is.euclid(distances): Zero distance(s)
#> $call
#> ade4::amova(samples = xtab, distances = xdist, structures = xstruct)

#>
#> $results
#>                  Df    Sum Sq   Mean Sq

#> Between samples   4  51.73143 12.932858
#> Within samples  123 508.15919  4.131376
#> Total           127 559.89062  4.408588
#>
#> $componentsofcovariance
#>                                 Sigma          %
#> Variations  Between samples 0.3468564   7.745388
#> Variations  Within samples  4.1313756  92.254612
#> Total variations            4.4782320 100.000000
#>
#> $statphi
#>                          Phi
#> Phi-samples-total 0.07745388

I hope that addresses your concerns. Don't hesitate to respond to this thread if you have any further questions.

Best,
Zhian
